title: An explicit version in a changeset overrides the computed bump
expectation: A changeset may pin an exact version instead of naming a severity. The object form carries `version` alongside `bump` and `type`, and the pinned version wins over the computed one: the group sits at 2.3.1, so a computed minor would plan 2.4.0, but an explicit 2.5.0 must plan 2.5.0. The same pin works through `monochange create --version`, which writes the `version` key into the frontmatter, and `--dry-run` previews the rendered file without writing anything.

setupFiles..changeset/explicit.md:
---
"@acme/api":
  bump: minor
  type: feat
  version: "2.5.0"
---

Rework the request input object

checks.why: The pinned version must win over the computed one. A computed minor on the 2.3.1 group would plan 2.4.0, so planning 2.5.0 proves the explicit value was honored rather than recomputed.
Guards the same assertion from the other side: if 2.4.0 (the computed minor) also appeared, the pin would not actually be in control of the plan.
The object form with `bump`, `type`, and `version` together is valid release intent.

checks.command: rm -f .changeset/created-*.md; monochange create --package @acme/api --version 2.5.0 --reason "Rework the request input" >/dev/null 2>&1; grep -l 'version: "2.5.0"' .changeset/*.md >/dev/null; rc=$?; rm -f .changeset/*.md; exit $rc
checks.why: The `--version` input must reach the file as the explicit `version` key, not be dropped in favor of a computed bump. The created file is removed so later checks start clean.

checks.command: monochange create --package @acme/api --version 2.5.0 --reason "Rework the request input" --dry-run > .dry.out 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -q 'Would create changeset' .dry.out; grep_rc=$?; count=$(ls .changeset/*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); rm -f .dry.out .changeset/*.md; test $rc -eq 0 -a $grep_rc -eq 0 -a "$count" = "0"
checks.why: Dry-run must preview the render and write nothing. This pins the freshly fixed behavior on the path most likely to regress, because `--version` changes what the rendered file looks like.
